dataPartitionPolicy.userDecision: Use GMBA outlines for data/graph preparation regions, keeping each whole whenever it is reasonably sized. Within oversized regions, prioritize and keep the most major through-highway cuts, then make the fewest additional lower-tier cuts needed. The user delegates the engineering size measure and accepts prompting for missing prepared-data downloads. Hikes crossing applied highway dividers are outside the accepted search scope, including pedestrian bridges and underpasses.
dataPartitionPolicy.status: Prepared and locally installed all five existing Washington Cascades sections on 2026-10-06 with no unavailable sections. The reviewed 700,000-segment capacity and I-90, US 12, US 2 and SR 20 cuts are unchanged; SR 410 remains unused. Earlier preparation-policy evidence remains in benchmarks/mountain-preparation-review.json.
dataPartitionPolicy.partitionTrigger: Keep a GMBA region whole up to 700,000 relevant consecutive OSM source-node pairs, before corridor compression. Count once per source segment regardless of walking direction; include admitted trails and road connectors. Duplicate source ways and unresolved barriers conservatively overcount. A cut requires both a currently oversized piece and a genuine available highway divider. The default is calibrated with real preparation and loaded-graph/search observations; it is a capacity proxy, not a guarantee for arbitrary future sources or query durations.
dataPartitionPolicy.cutSelection: Engineering default under the user's delegated choice: apply the size gate first. For an oversized GMBA region, retain all suitable through-freeway dividers, then choose the fewest additional approved lower-tier highway cuts needed to bring the pieces under the size threshold. Prefer more significant corridors and lower largest-piece workload when equally small selections are feasible. Do not cut a small region merely because a highway exists. Never introduce an artificial divider when an oversized piece has no suitable highway; report that unresolved preparation capacity instead.
proposedWorkflow: Identify a named GMBA region to add within supported coverage.
For an oversized region, identify highway corridors that actually divide it. Prioritize through-freeways and minimize the additional lower-tier cuts needed.

dataPartitionPolicy.candidateRule: Follow continuous mainline highway corridors, using numbered route identity and road-network significance to generate candidates. A selected corridor must form a closed region together with the preparation footprint or other selected dividers; do not invent continuations from road endpoints. Review actual mainline geometry, divided carriageways, junctions and route-reference changes before selection.
dataPartitionPolicy.selectionEvidence: Compare the largest resulting preparation workload, retained trail networks and starts, and excluded independently known hike families. Prefer a small reviewed set of substantial dividers; neither geographic area nor OSM highway class alone is sufficient.

loopGroupingDecision.approved: Group similar main circuits for display; retain exact circuit versions with their own qualifying starts and directions. User authorizes the initial path-difference judgment and later tuning.
loopGroupingDecision.policy: Choose the preferred qualifying route for each exact circuit first. Process circuits in the existing route-preference order. Attach each circuit to the most similar qualifying displayed loop already chosen, or show it as a new hike if none qualifies. Share at least 60% of the longer physical main circuit, including roads, after removing the retraced approach; shared paths must have the same cyclic order. Keep displayed routes fixed. Existing route preference resolves tied matches. Every version must match its displayed loop; versions need not all match one another. No two displayed loops can meet this rule.
loopGroupingDecision.persistence: Grouping does not discard distinct circuits. New completed jobs save their grouping explanation. Existing completed files remain immutable and readable under their original grouping.

profileGradeDecision.approved: Show signed percent grade beside hover distance and altitude in the existing elevation profile readout.
